A 24-year-old male with a history of IV drug use, alcohol abuse, and antisocial personality disorder
comes to the emergency department reporting back pain that began yesterday and has progressively
worsened. He reports general weakness and feeling unwell. He is requesting IV diphenhydramine and
hydromorphone. His vital signs show: - Temperature: 101°F (38.3°C) - Blood pressure: 102/78 mmHg -
Pulse: 101/min - Respirations: 19/min - Oxygen saturation: 99% on room air Physical examination
reveals focal tenderness over the lumbar spine, with normal neurological and musculoskeletal exams.
Laboratory results show: Hematology: - Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL - Hematocrit: 36% - Leukocyte count:
11,500/mm³ with normal differential - Platelet count: 397,000/mm³ Serum: - Na■: 137 mEq/L - Cl■: 103
mEq/L - K■: 4.8 mEq/L - HCO■■: 25 mEq/L - BUN: 24 mg/dL - Glucose: 79 mg/dL - Creatinine: 1.1
mg/dL - Ca²■: 10.2 mg/dL - ESR: 49 mm/hr - AST: 202 U/L - ALT: 101 U/L The patient threatens to

leave if not given IV pain medications. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
Psychogenic pain disorder (B) Musculoskeletal strain (C) Malingering (D) Acute osteomyelitis (E)
Spinal epidural abscess (F) Septic arthritis (G) Drug-seeking behavior (H) Factitious disorder (I) Spinal
epidural hematoma (J) Acute disc herniation
